lesson.title: Telling Time to the Nearest 5 Minutes
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you measured length. Today, measure something different: time!

On a clock, the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. Each small mark around the clock represents 5 minutes, so you can read the time by counting by 5s as the long hand moves: 5, 10, 15, 20... Practice reading these times: the long hand pointing straight down (6, meaning 30 minutes past the hour), and the long hand pointing at the 3 (meaning 15 minutes past the hour). Draw or describe a clock showing 4:15 and a clock showing 7:45.
You just practiced reading time to the nearest 5 minutes — a real skill you'll use every day! Tomorrow we'll measure something else: money.

objectives: Read the time on an analog clock to the nearest 5 minutes
Draw or describe a clock showing a given time
materialsNeeded: A real or paper clock with movable hands, if available
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's length-measurement work.
2. Introduce reading the clock's hour and minute hands, counting by 5s for minutes.
3. Practice reading 2-3 example times together.
4. Have the child draw clocks for 4:15 and 7:45.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Close by checking the current real time on a clock together.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the easiest landmark times (:00, :15, :30, :45) before reading arbitrary 5-minute marks
Ready for more: ask the child to figure out what time it will be in 20 minutes from a given starting time
A real clock with movable hands makes this lesson far more concrete than a static worksheet image alone
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a clock-reading and drawing activity — check that the child correctly draws the hour hand near the 4 and minute hand at the 3 (for 4:15), and the hour hand near the 8 and minute hand at the 9 (for 7:45).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 2 standard 2.MD.7: telling and writing time from analog clocks to the nearest 5 minutes, continuing this week's measurement theme.

worksheet.title: Telling Time to the Nearest 5 Minutes

generationData.instructions: Draw or describe a clock showing each time.
